new_statements.translation: 2.1.1. The phonological status of the vowels has not been determined. On the basis of the existing materials the following vowel inventory is posited for the south-western zone [...] 2.1.2. Stress usually falls on the last long vowel. 2.1.3. There may be a connection between aspiration and vowel tone in the south-eastern dialects (rising tone next to aspirated consonants). Other positionally conditioned realizations of phonemes have not been studied. 2.1.4. Syllable structure has not been studied.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress normally goes to the rightmost long vowel of the word (quantity-driven, right-oriented, unbounded); what happens in words with no long vowel is not stated. Stated for Pashai as a whole, in a sketch whose phonology is drawn from Morgenstierne's (largely Laurowan/NW) materials.
new_statements.exceptions: Only the hedge 'usually' (obychno); no lexical exceptions listed. A possible aspiration-linked rising tone is mentioned for south-eastern dialects only.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level statement in an encyclopedic grammar sketch; no discussion of phrase stress or citation forms. Second-hand: the article's bibliography is Buddruss 1959, Edelman 1983 and Morgenstierne 1944/1956/1967, and 2.1.1 says the phonology is posited 'from existing materials'.
new_statements.identity_note: The only stress rule found (Grjunberg 1999) is stated for Pashai as a whole (family-level pash1270, covering all four ISO Pashayi languages); the article explicitly includes the north-western group (Gulbahar and parts of Alingar/Alishang) but its data are compiled from Morgenstierne, whose principal informants came from Laurowan (Glottolog laur1248) and Kohnadeh/Satha near Gulbahar (kohn1238) - both dialects of Northwest Pashayi nort2665 - so Morgenstierne 1967 is the on-target primary grammar. The first-hand statement in Nawata 1985 is for the Kordar (= Kurdar, kurd1258) dialect, which Glottolog places under Northeast Pashayi nort2666, not the target. Lamuwal & Baker 2013 and Strand's Degano page describe Southeast Pashayi (sout2672). Note Edelman 1983 calls Laurowan 'south-western group' in Morgenstierne's scheme, but Glottolog/Ethnologue list Laurowan under Northwest Pashayi.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p.161-162: 'Kyosei (sutoresu) wa, ippan ni gomatsu ni kuru' = stress generally comes at the end of the word; examples papus, tajyak, wacak, masik, mayak (final syllable). Vowel length not phonemic; tone status undetermined. Kordar = Kurdar dialect, Northeast Pashayi [aee]; own informant work, Kabul 1966-67.
